title: Directory federation with IAM roles
scenario: Tidewater Logistics Co-op has 140 dispatch and finance staff who sign in to Windows with credentials held in an on-premises Active Directory forest, and an AD FS farm already serves two internal web applications. Today it runs one AWS account and wants staff to reach the console with those same credentials, with no separate IAM users and no second password to remember. Within 18 months it plans about 12 accounts, one per business unit plus shared services, under one AWS Organization. The security lead has ruled that passwords must never be stored in or synchronized to AWS and that no domain controller may run in AWS. Two identity engineers will own whatever is built.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Decide between SAML 2.0 federation through AD FS (or another SAML IdP) and IAM Identity Center for the single-account case, and justify the choice

If IAM Identity Center is chosen for the single-account case, state that assigning AWS account access requires an organization instance (AWS Organizations enabled, with this account as the management account)

Compare AD Connector, AWS Managed Microsoft AD, and a per-account SAML identity provider as the identity source or federation mechanism for the multi-account case, and state, for each option, whether passwords stay on premises and whether it runs domain controllers in AWS
State whether IAM Identity Center is used in the multi-account case, and if so, what its identity source is
The security lead forbids synchronizing passwords to AWS and forbids running domain controllers in AWS
Two identity engineers must be able to operate the result; adding the twelfth account must not mean building a new trust from scratch
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions
